_comment: CANONICAL theme registry. Both the renderer and the web app read THIS file.
WHY IT EXISTS
D-163: five independent copies of the id -> name pairing existed and two of
them disagreed with the renderer on every single id. A user whose account
default was 4 (teal) had the wizard pre-select 'elegant'. Nothing compared
the copies, so nothing failed. This file is the one place the pairing is
stated; `tests/test_theme_registry_is_single_sourced.py` parses every other
site that still names a theme and asserts it agrees.
IDS ARE STABLE AND ARE NEVER REUSED
`accounts.default_theme_id`, `property_reports.theme` and the
`property_report_stats.theme_<name>` columns all hold historical values.
Renumbering 2/3/5 to 1/2/3 would silently relabel every report already
generated, so the retired ids stay retired and the gaps stay.
RETIRING IS NOT DELETING
A retired theme keeps its row below because the stats columns keep counting
the reports that were made with it. `accounts.default_theme_id` CHECK stays
1..5 for the same reason: tightening it to IN (2,3,5) would fail against
rows that already hold 1 and 4.
RENAMING IS NOT RETIRING, AND THE TWO LISTS ARE SEPARATE
`bold`, `elegant` and `modern` were renamed to `atlas`, `linen` and
`harbor` on 2026-10-13. Their IDS (5, 3, 2) ARE STILL LIVE and their
templates still exist — under new paths. So they do NOT belong in
`retired`, which means 'this id has no template and is not in use': a
retired entry for id 5 would make `resolve(5)` fall back to the default
and relabel every report an account on 5 has ever produced.
They go in `renamed` instead, which exists for one reason: a FORMER name
in live code is just as broken as a retired one, for a different cause.
`'bold'` now asks the renderer for `bold/bold_report.jinja2`, which the
rename moved. So `test_no_live_code_path_names_a_retired_theme` reads
retired names AND former names, and says which kind it found.
